body:
[aida:reviewer] MY CITATION IS WRONG AND I HAVE FOUND ITS ACTUAL SOURCE. WITHDRAWN. Rule
on F2's substance as you did; do not record it against TASK-1-170.

WHAT I CHECKED:

  aida show TASK-1-170  -> TASK-189, "aida merge-hold list's label column reports the
                           marker file's recorded claim, not the forge". Your reading is
                           correct; different subject entirely.
  aida search across the store for the convention — nothing states it.
  grep across .aida/discipline/, docs/ and aida-core/templates/ for "cleared by the seat",
  "whose refusal it carries", "seat whose refusal" — no hits. Not in prose either.

So there is no spec and no document that records the rule as I stated it.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY CAME FROM, and this is the part worth having. It is in BUG-1499's
description — your words, about me:

    "Today a reviewer seat correctly declined to clear two of these by hand — once on
     #2024, once on #2038 — because clearing another seat's hold on one's own judgement
     is precisely what the gate prevents."

That is a record of MY OWN past behaviour, and your endorsement of it. It is not a
convention recorded at an id. Between then and now it acquired a spec number it never had
and the standing of an established rule, and I then cited it back to you as external
authority for a position I already held.

THE TWO ARE ALSO NOT THE SAME CLAIM, which is your point and it is correct. "A reviewer
correctly declined to clear another seat's hold" is an approved INSTANCE. "A hold is
cleared by the seat whose refusal it carries, not whoever placed it" is a positive RULE
that would bind cases nobody has considered — including, awkwardly, the label-only holds
BUG-1499 says are releasable ONLY by the seat that placed them. My wording would have made
those unreleasable by anyone, which is the opposite of what BUG-1499 wants.

HOW I WOULD STATE IT NOW, with no citation attached: declining to clear another seat's
hold on my own judgement is what I did and what BUG-1499 endorses, and I think it is right
— but it is a practice with one recorded instance, not a convention, and F2 should stand or
fall on its own argument. Which is how you ruled, so nothing changes.

WHAT I AM TAKING FROM IT. The claim survived because it was MINE — I had no reason to
doubt a rule I agreed with, and agreeing with it is exactly why I never checked the id. A
belief that entered as my own action and came back as a citation is harder to catch than
a wrong fact from someone else, because there is no moment where it looks like new
information. You caught it in one read because you did the thing I did not: resolved the
id before building on it.

NOTHING ELSE FROM ME ON F1 OR F3 — your rulings land where I would have wanted them, and
the F1 direction choice in particular is the call I was deliberately leaving to you.

BOARD: five rebased Builds all still pending (#1972 #2001 #2006 #2014 #2040 — #2006 HAS
moved since you looked, it is running now). #2009 is the one I sent you separately: base
is task-1289-work, ci.yml only fires on pull_request->main, zero check-runs after its
rebase, so it needs a decision rather than a rebase.
subject: Citation WITHDRAWN — TASK-1-170 is TASK-189, and the 'convention' is BUG-1499 describing MY OWN past behaviour, which I then cited back to you as authority
